title: Bikeability | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Bikeability cycle training
What is Bikeability?
Bikeability is 'cyclist training' for the 21st century, designed to give the next generation of riders the skills and confidence to ride their bikes on today’s roads.
We constantly review our 'offer' and have a suite of Bikeability training that we can offer schools, community groups and members of the public.
Bikeability 1,2 and 3
Half term and holiday training
We encourage participants to bring their own bike, as that is the bike that they are familiar with. However we have a fleet of bikes that are available for primary school age children if they do not have access to one of their own. We can also access adapted bikes for riders that may have special needs through our partner organisations. You do not have to be able to ride already to participate in our training offer but you do need to make us aware so that we can support you.
A child in the Bradford District will typically start Bikeability lessons in years 4, 5, 6 or 7, progressing through Level 1 in their first session and then completing Level 2 in sessions 2 and 3. Certificates and shiny luminous badges are awarded to children who successfully complete each level. Level 3 can be completed when the cyclist has gained more experience of cycling.
In a school setting our team of instructors have the flexibility to tailor the training to fit the school and pupils. When we are onsite and in dialogue with teachers we will adapt the programme to best fit the development of the participants. We will encourage progression through as many of the levels as is possible within the skill set of the pupil and the time frame given.
Bikeability was developed by more than 20 professional organisations including the Royal Society for Prevention against Accidents and is supported by cross-Government departments including the Department for Transport, Department of Health and Department for Children, Schools and Families.
So far, millions of young cyclists have been trained across the country and thousands of coveted Bikeability badges have been awarded. The ultimate vision is that no child should leave primary school without the opportunity to take part in Bikeability training.
There’s a Bikeability level to match every ability, whether you’re just starting out or already have some good skills and just want to use your bike more safely and more often. You might start from the beginning at Level 1 and train all the way through to Level 3, or you might dive in with Level 3 if you already have lots of cycling experience. It’s important to remember that there’s always something new to learn, and that the right level of Bikeability training will help you to develop the best habits that will keep you safe whenever you cycle.
During Level 1, you learn to control and master your bike. The training takes place in an environment away from cars or traffic - usually in a playground or closed car park.
During Level 2, you will get out on to the roads. Level 2 gives you the confidence and cycling experience so the you are able to deal with traffic on short journeys such as cycling to school or to friends.
During Level 3, you will gain the skills and confidence to tackle busier roads. It deals with route planning and, depending on what you need, can include roundabouts, A roads, traffic lights, filtering through slow or stationary traffic and turning into multi-lane roads.
If you are interested in becoming a Bikeability school please contact the Road Safety team on 01274 437409 or email roadsafety@bradford.gov.uk.
How much does Bikeability training cost?
Training is generally free of charge but schools must fulfil certain criteria (see below).
How long will the training take?
The Combined Level 1 and 2 course is 9 hours long and is generally delivered over 2 school days. The course can be delivered over a different time frame in consultation with the Co-ordinator. The Level 3 training is structured differently please contact the Co-ordinator for further information. Remember further adaptations can be accommodated when we are on site.
Does the school need to assist with the running of a Bikeability course?
Yes. A school must send out permission slips and other associated paperwork and provide assistance where a child may have a disability or learning need. Further information can be found on the Bikeability cycling training for schools web page.
What equipment is needed?
The children need to bring their own working bike and helmet. We can often loan bikes and helmets for children to borrow but they are subject to availability. If equipment is borrowed it will stay on the school site for the duration of the training. We also support children with special needs please inform either the co-ordinator or the instructors.
How many children can a school have trained?
A school must provide a minimum of 10 children for a course to run but for efficiency 12 children is best. There are no limits to the number of courses a school can book within a year.
Are there any booklets available with course?
Bikeability supporting information will now be online please visit the Bikeability news web page.

title: Cycling to work | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Cycle park facilities
Cycle park facilities are available at railway stations in the district. Information about taking your bike on the train can be found on the West Yorkshire Metro website.
Bradford Council also provide bike parking including secure lockers available to hire for more information can be found on the Bicycle Parking webpage.
Support for people who cycle to work or want to start cycling
The CityConnect programme offers a range of ways for both businesses and their employees to get into cycling.
Bradford also has a cyclists' forum which meets quarterly and is open to all who wish to have a voice in the Bradford cycling community.
If you're interested in cycling as a commuter or for recreation take a look at the British Cycling website for all sorts of interesting advice and news.
Leeds Bradford Cycle Superhighway is a segregated cycle route between Leeds and Bradford, running from Leeds city centre along the A647 to the new Broadway shopping centre right in the heart of Bradford. The highway offers the opportunity to cycle and walk, away from the traffic.
The Canal Road Cycleway is a segregated cycle route running from Bradford City Centre on Canal Road past Foster Square Retail Park to Stanley Road where it joins the Canal Road Greenway an off road cycleway that takes you to Leeds Road in Shipley.
The West Bradford Cycle Super highway starts in the City Centre running along Sunbridge Road where it then continues along Thornton Road to just west of the A6177 Ring Road and is due to open in Summer 2025. There are plans to extend this to Thornton subject to funding.
National Cycle Network
Route 66 connects Shipley via the City Centre to the Spen Valley Greenway which then provides off road cycle route to Cleckheaton and onto Dewsbury.
The canal towpath Route NCN69/696/66 provides an off road cycle route between Silsden and Leeds via Riddlesden, Bingley, Saltaire, Shipley and Apperley Bridge.
Find out more on the National Cycle Network OS map.

title: Inclusive Fitness Initiative | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Membership and prices
Inclusive Fitness Initiative
Inclusive Fitness Initiative (IFI) is a programme supporting the fitness industry to become more inclusive, catering for the needs of disabled and non-disabled people, raising physical activity participation levels.
Everyone, whatever their age, gender or activity levels, can enjoy physical activity. Sometimes starting the process is difficult and many people put up barriers or make excuses. Below is information that may help you take up some sort of activity with us.
Many of our sports centres run specific activities and sessions for people with all fitness levels and with different personal needs. Contact your local centre to find out that what they have on offer.
The ClubActive gyms at The Leisure Centre, Keighley and Thornton Recreation Centre all have a wide array of IFI accredited equipment.
Going to the facility for the first time can be daunting. The experience can be confusing so we have put together a few helpful bits of information that we hope will encourage you to join us at one of our facilities. It is time to be active, get healthy and have fun.
What should I expect?
Don’t feel intimidated or worried that everyone else will know what they are doing. Your gym instructor at your induction will help you with the equipment and explain what you will be doing. Don’t worry about remembering everything you have been told at your first visit, instructors will always be on hand to help and advise you.
Something sensible that you feel comfortable in. Designer outfits are not required!
What do I need to take when I go?
Something to drink from whilst you exercise
A small towel to wipe yourself and the gym machines down
Change for the lockers
Is going to the gym enough?
Not if you sit in the sauna or café area all the time! Take advice from the instructors and try and make your sessions as productive as possible.
Only set yourself SMART objectives/goals
Specific - Objectives should specify what you want to achieve
Measurable - You should be able to measure whether you are meeting your objectives
Achievable - Are the objectives you set achievable?
Realistic - Can you realistically achieve your objectives?
Timed - When do you want to achieve by?

title: New sports centres | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Why do we need new sports facilities?
A number of Bradford’s existing sport and leisure centres are coming to the end of their life-span and are considered no longer fit for purpose. Some of the District’s facilities now represent a financial burden to the Council due to rising running and maintenance costs. In these times of austerity the Council needs to look how it best provides services today, but also to ensure that we have can provide for future generations.
The proposed new leisure centres
We will provide two new, exciting, modern leisure centres that will encourage even more people to take up physical activity. By building these new modern leisure facilities we can deliver a greatly improved experience for leisure centre customers as well as significantly reduce running costs.
The new sports facilities will be located to better serve Bradford’s residents. Every community should be within a reasonable distance of a high quality leisure centre.
This programme of facility development will result in some of our older facilities closing. We have made a commitment that new facilities will open before the outdated facilities close. Proceeds from the sale of these old sites will help to pay for the new facilities.
The new facilities will be delivered one after another.
The first facility to be delivered was Sedbergh Sports and Leisure Centre, which opened in November 2019.
Design work for the Squire Lane development began in late 2017.

Sport and activities
Paddle and Pause (adults only)
The Paddle and Pause sessions are adult only kayak and paddleboard sessions, for those wanting to take a “Pause” from their day and do something for themselves.
These sessions are open to people of any ability. Whether you are a complete novice wanting to try something new, or a regular paddler wanting to meet like-minded people or just get out for a few laps around the reservoir, then these sessions are just for you.
We will have staff on hand to either just give you the basics and get you out on the water or give you a little more tuition - it's entirely up to you.
Looking after your health and wellbeing is now becoming the focus of many of our lives and getting out on the water in our beautiful surroundings is the perfect tonic.
Sit on top kayaks and paddleboards will be available on each session, and both are suitable for novices although paddleboarding does tend to be the wetter of the two! Just pick the craft you want to hire when you book.
We want to create a welcoming and friendly atmosphere for these sessions and along with the abundance of fun and laughter we tend to get during the actual session, we will also have hot drinks available for after each session (tea fund donations welcome). This gives participants chance to chat to staff and each other after the session.
Do you think your workplace would benefit from a session like this?
Contact us at doe.park@bradford.gov.uk to discuss booking a team session!

Centre staff will be on hand to offer guidance and tuition on these sessions if requested at the start of the session.
For participants wishing to independently paddle you are free to do so following a basic safety brief for any first-time visitors to the centre regardless of experience.
Paddlesport activities carry inherent risks, which cannot be entirely eliminated; in particular, those associated with cold water. Participants must be aware of and accept the risks, whilst taking responsibility for actions which minimise the risks to acceptable levels.
The following rules will help to keep activities safe and enjoyable for all:
All participants must always wear a buoyancy aid once they enter the waterfront area. These are provided and included in the cost for all hire and launch bookings.
Wetsuits are strongly recommended for anyone hiring a stand-up paddleboard. These are issued free of charge.
If you do not wish to wear a wetsuit, please wear light weight quick drying clothing suitable for the weather on the day. You will get splashed whilst paddling.
Participants paddling independently must ensure that their activities are within their own ability and confidence levels and appropriate to the prevailing weather conditions. If you are unsure, you are welcome to stay under the guidance of centre staff for the duration of the session.
Participants who are launching their own craft must ensure they are well maintained. We do not allow launching of inflatable novelty pool floats, lilos or inflatable rowing boats. If you are unsure, please contact us.
There is no swimming allowed, if you fall out of your craft please get back on immediately or in an emergency signal to be rescued. Anyone found to be not adhering to this rule or continuously capsizing will be asked to leave immediately and may be unable to book on any further sessions.

Paddlesport activities carry inherent risks, which cannot be entirely eliminated; in particular, those associated with cold water. Participants must be aware of and accept the risks, whilst taking responsibility for actions which minimise the risks to acceptable levels.
General rules and safety information
The following information will help to keep activities safe and enjoyable for all:
All participants must always wear a buoyancy aid once they enter the waterfront area. These are provided and included in the cost.
Wetsuits are strongly recommended (particularly for all under 18’s and anyone hiring a paddleboard). These are issued free of charge.
Please come “beach ready” just to put these on. If you do not wish to wear a wetsuit, please wear light weight quick drying clothing suitable for the weather on the day.
All paddleboards must have the leash always attached to their waist or ankle when on the water.
Passengers are not allowed on paddleboards. Please book enough craft for the participants attending.
The wearing of footwear is recommended whilst participating. We cannot accept responsibility for any footwear left around the launching area.
Participants must ensure that their activities are within their own ability and confidence levels and appropriate to the prevailing weather conditions.
Rotating participants around one craft for either a hire or launch booking is not allowed. Please book enough craft for people attending.
Under 18’s must be accompanied by an adult participating with them.
1 adult can supervise up to two under 18s
Children under the age of 8 must be in the same craft as an adult. Minimum age is 5.
Adults must be confident that any children hiring single boats or boards are confident and able enough to paddle independently. If you are unsure book a tandem craft for their first session.
Participants who are launching their own craft must ensure they are well maintained. We do not allow launching of inflatable novelty pool floats, lilos or inflatable rowing boats. If you are unsure, please contact us.
There is no swimming allowed, if you fall out of your craft please get back on immediately or in an emergency signal to be rescued. Anyone found to be not adhering to this rule or continuously capsizing will be asked to leave immediately and may be unable to book on any further sessions.
You will have full use of the reservoir for the session but on occasion there may be a need to set boundaries (prevailing weather conditions, reservoir overflow) These boundaries must be adhered to for the duration of the session.
The banks around the reservoir are rocky and unstable. You must not disembark on any banks around the reservoir other than the designated launching area by the pontoons.
Please respect the equipment provided to you and do not drag boards or boats across the bank. You will be charged for any damage caused to equipment whilst on your hire.
Smoking, drugs and alcohol are prohibited.
Emergency safety boat cover will be available on site; however, this will be for emergency recovery only.
It is at the management's discretion to refuse hire or ask you to leave if the above rules or boundaries on the water are not adhered to. In this case refunds will not be given.

title: Physical Contact Statement | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Physical Contact Statement
Important information to parents and children participating in diving lessons and coaching classes.
Further to recent NSPCC advice, we are required to inform you that there are aspects of our teaching, which require a “hands on” technique.
This type of physical contact between teachers and divers will only be used in full view of the balcony and the class and will only be used for the following reasons:
Where it is essential to support the diver during the early stages of learning a skill for safety reasons
To develop the skill and technique (eg placing the diver in the correct position/posture)
To prevent an injury (eg pushing them away from the poolside if, during the process of the dive the teacher considers them to be too close to the poolside)
To treat an injury (only relates to staff who are first aid qualified)
Please let us know on joining the programme, if you are uncomfortable with any aspect of this teaching technique.

title: Swimming policies and regulations | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Swimming policies and regulations
Swimmers Code of Conduct
We are committed to providing all our customers with a quality service in a friendly, clean and safe environment. To help us achieve this please observe our Swimmers Code of Conduct at all times:
Wear only appropriate, recognised swimwear.
Babies and young children should wear only appropriate elasticated swimwear.
Shower thoroughly and toilet before entering the pool
Follow all instructions given by staff and displayed on notices, safety signs etc
Behave in a responsible and courteous manner to all staff and other customers.
Pay due respect to the safety and enjoyment of all customers.
Treat the facility with care and respect.
Stay in shallow water if you cannot swim well.
Never leave children under 8 years of age unsupervised and always comply with the ‘Children in Swimming Pools Policy’.
You are suffering or have recently suffered with diarrhoea or a gastro-intestinal infection.
You have a medical problem (without first consulting your doctor).
You have recently consumed alcohol or a main meal.
Children in Swimming Pools Policy
Children under the age of 8 years will not be admitted to the Swimming Pool unless accompanied in the water at all times by a responsible person of 16 years or over.
The responsible person should maintain a constant watch over the children for whom they are responsible and be in close contact with those of their children who are weak or non-swimmers.
Children aged between 4-7 years must be accompanied by a responsible person on a maximum Two to One basis.
We strongly recommend that all children under 4 are accompanied on a One to One basis and remain in shallow water at all times regardless of swimming ability. Buoyancy aids are available on loan free of charge, to all children under 4, in all pools, at all times.
Please abide by the Swimmers Code of Conduct and the Children in Swimming Pools Policy at all times, it is conditional to your admission to the pool.
All inclusive swim slide policy
The slides are not recommended for people with ill health.
Opening hours vary during school/bank holidays.
During busy periods, your time in the pool could be limited to one hour.
Facility Management, Sports Development, Play and Adventure Activities are committed to providing a varied and balanced service of the highest quality that meets the needs and expectations of the communities we serve.
Therefore we promise that:
We will provide an environment which is friendly, clean and safe.
We will implement and maintain a quality system where appropriate.
We will strive to provide value for money.
We will comply with current legislation and regulations as appropriate.
We will have clear technical standards for all important features of the service and meet them.
Customer communications:
We will encourage customers to comment when their expectations have not been met and will be responsive to comments, complaints and suggestions.
We will publish customer comments and the management response in all facilities.
We will undertake regular surveys and consultation of our customers and potential customers to ensure that we continue to meet their identified needs.
We will ensure that accurate customer information on all activities, including times, prices and availability of sessions, courses etc will be available for customers.
Any foreseen changes will be notified to customers by the display of an appropriate notice within the facility.
Will be trained and appropriately qualified.
Will work in a helpful, informed, courteous and professional manner at all times.
Will be easily identifiable by wearing their uniform at all times.
Will be in good working order and checked and maintained regularly.
Will be set up in accordance with the requirements of the manufacturer and / or governing body of the sport where necessary.
Will be ready for use as soon as practical for the commencement of the booked period.
Will be regularly checked by staff and remedial action taken where necessary.
We will strive to continually seek ways of improving and developing services.
We would appreciate your comments on the above.

Sport and activities
Community Sports and Activities Development Unit
Tackling inactivity is the key focus area for our Community Sports and Activities Development Unit.
Our aim is to work together with partners to enable the people of the Bradford district from the youngest to the oldest, to live active and healthier lives in their communities, particularly where the need is greatest.
The long-term aim is to provide people with support to enjoy a lifelong involvement in physical, health and sport initiatives. Our aims are to:
increase participation in physical activity and sport
reduce health inequalities
improve social cohesion
deliver holiday activities
organise and deliver events for the benefit of the district
support clubs, communities and individuals
The Community Sports and Activities Development Unit delivers a number of other initiatives to develop physical sporting and health opportunities for people of all ages, levels of interest and ability.

title: Dance For Life | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Dance for Life are a Bradford based project which sits in Bradford Council, that offer classes, workshops, after school clubs, performance opportunities, a dance company and dance training schemes across the Bradford district in many different styles of dance.
Set up in 1992 by Cathy Middleton with the idea of improving young people’s health and well-being through dance, Dance for Life now works in schools, youth clubs, gyms and community centres across the district providing sessions and workshops that cater for all. Dance is a great activity, not only for its health and fitness benefits, improving your confidence, co-ordination, strength and flexibility but it is also a fantastic social activity!
As well as workshops and classes Dance for Life also has a small performance team who regularly perform at events throughout the area. All dancers are expertly trained and highly accomplished; the performance team is renowned for putting on a great show!

Live to Dance - Dance for life
We offer inclusive classes, workshops, holiday camps, afterschool clubs, mixed ability classes, performance opportunities and dance training schemes across Bradford district in all dance styles.
Dance is a great activity, not only for its health and fitness benefits, improving you confidence, co-ordination, strength and flexibility but it is also a fantastic social activity and is fun!
These sessions help young children learn and communicate through their bodies by encouraging brain development. we aim to focus on the role of dance, movement and play to support physical, social and emotional development in early childhood, as well as having lots of fun!
It is about providing young children with an enjoyable foundation in the principles of dance, movement and performance.
Primary School Dance sessions
We offer dance classes, workshops, after school clubs, performance opportunities and teachers training screams across the district in different styles of dance.
Dance is a great physical activities, not only for its Health and fitness benefits, but also improves confidence, co-ordination, strength and flexibility.
We work with schools to personally tailor their dance experience for children. This can be part of the curriculum or after school.

title: Sports and activities camps | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Sports and activities camps
An indoor sports and activities camp during the half-term holidays offers an exciting and engaging opportunity for children aged 5 to 14 years old to stay active, learn new skills, and have fun while staying warm and dry. These camps typically feature a variety of sports, such as football, cricket, basketball, dodgeball, badminton, dance, and team-building exercises.
With professional and qualified coaching staff and a focus on skill development, children not only improve their physical abilities but also boost their confidence, teamwork, and social skills. The camp environment is safe, supportive, and designed to keep kids entertained while allowing parents peace of mind. title: Bradford Aquatics Competition Development programme | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Bradford Aquatics Competition Development programme
Welcome to Bradford Aquatics Competition Development programme for the aquatic disciplines of swimming and diving. The swimming and diving programmes are managed by Bradford Aquatics department of Bradford Metropolitan District Council. The aims of the competition programmes are Athlete Development from the ages of 8 in swimming and 6 in diving. Both programmes run in accordance with the Amateur Swimming Association's ‘Long Term Athlete Development Plan’ which encourages its participants to success from fundamentals right the way through to training to win.
Participation in the program is by invitation following talent identification (TID) through school swimming, school PE lessons, local clubs and swimming and diving lessons.
The Competition programmes are run in conjunction with the City of Bradford Swimming Club and City of Bradford Esprit Diving Club, each club coordinates the competitive element that compliments the athletes training.
It is important to remember that the coaches are employed by Bradford Aquatics and not by the club.
The scheme is focussed on competitive development and the training. For the competitive side the participants are required to be members of the appropriate discipline’s club (City of Bradford SC and the Bradford Esprit Diving club). These are separate entities to the scheme and must be joined individually. The swimmers and divers are expected to compete and train as each squad criteria states.
Long Term Athlete Development (LTAD) is a sports development framework that is based on human growth and development. LTAD it is about adopting an athlete centred approach to development. All young people follow the same pattern of growth from infancy through adolescence, but there are significant individual differences in both the timing and magnitude of the changes that take place. It is however important to stress that human growth and development happens without training, however training can enhance all of the changes that take place.

title: Bradford Aquatics swim school membership contract conditions | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Bradford Aquatics swim school membership contract conditions - December 2024
1. These Contract Conditions
1.1 What these Contract Conditions cover
These are the terms and conditions on which we, the Council, will supply Swimming Services to you, the Consumer, under the Contract between us.
1.2 Why you should read them
Please read these Contract Conditions carefully before you sign the Application Form. These tell you who we are, how we will provide the Swimming Services to you, how you and we may change, suspend, end or cancel the Contract, what to do if there is a problem and other important information. If you think that there is a mistake in these Contract Conditions or you are not clear what they mean, please contact us to discuss.
The capitalised words and expressions referred to in the Contract have the following meanings:
"Adult" means the category of Member aged at least 16 years of age.
" Aquatot" means the category of Member aged up to 4 years of age.
"Application Form" means each application form for Swimming Services completed and signed by or on behalf of the Member.
"BASS" means Bradford Aquatic Swim School.
"BASS Membership Card" means the membership card issued to each Member who has paid the Fee for the Swimming Services.
"Benefit" means the vouchers and other benefits provided by the Council, at its discretion, to Members who have commenced payment of the Fee for Swimming Services.
"Bradford Aquatic Website" means the Council's website detailing the Swimming Services, Fees, the Benefits provided by the Council, the Pool Facilities, the contact details of the BASS team and other useful information as amended from time to time at www.bradford.gov.uk/sport-and-activities/swimming/swimming-lessons-with-bradford-aquatics
"Bradford Leisure Card" means the card issued by the Council which entitles cardholders to reduced admission costs to a number of leisure activities in the Bradford District, including the Swimming Services.
"Cancellation Period" means a period of 14 days after, but not including the Commencement Date and if the last day of that period is not a Working Day then that period shall be extended to the next Working Day.
"Commencement Date" means the date the Contract is created in accordance with the Notice sent to you by the Council as referred to in clause 3.1.
"Complaint" means any complaint in Writing from any person who feels aggrieved by the Council's provision of Swimming Services or any breach by the Council of any of its obligations under the Contract.
"Consumer" (you, your)" means the person whom enters into the Contract as a Member or any person signing on behalf of a Junior Member.
"Contract" means the contract entered into between the Consumer and the Council incorporating the Application Form and these Contract Conditions.
"Contract Conditions" means these contract conditions known and described as the Bradford Aquatic Swim School Membership Contract Conditions (as amended from time to time).
"Contract Period" means the period of the Contract from the Commencement Date until the Contract comes to an end as referred to at clause 6.1.
"Council (we, our)" means City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council
"Customer Code of Conduct" means the rules of conduct of the Pool Facility attended by the Member as displayed at and obtained from the relevant Pool Facility.
"Fee" means the VAT exempt fees from time to time charged to the Consumer by the Council for the Swimming Services subject to any available discount applied to the holders of a valid Bradford Leisure Card.
"Junior" means the category of Member of between 5-15 years of age.
"Member" means a member of BASS who has entered into this Agreement, who has paid for Swimming Services and who are issued with a BASS Membership Card.
"Month" means calendar month.
"Notice" means a notice sent in Writing.
"Pool Facility" means the swimming pool venue in the district of Bradford as referred to at the Bradford Aquatic Website at which the Member has elected to receive Swimming Services.
"RPI" means the Retail Price Index.
"Senior Citizen" means a Member aged at least 65 years.
"Swimming Courses" means the categories of swimming courses or lessons from time to time provided by the Council to Members which are dependent on the available activities at a Pool Facility, the age of the Member, the number of participants in a lesson and the time the lessons are taken in any Week, details of which are available at any Pool Facility and on the Bradford Aquatic Website
"Swim Wear Policy" means the Council's requirements regarding the swim wear to be worn at the Pool Facilities.
"Week" means seven consecutive days.
"Working Day" means any day excluding Saturdays and Sundays, Bank Holidays and any designated public holidays including Good Friday and Christmas Day.
"Writing" means by way of emails, subject to proof of receipt for otherwise by post or a Notice hand-delivered to any Pool Facility.
Information about us and how to contact us
BASS is a Service of City of Bradford Metropolitan District Council of City Hall, Bradford BD1 1HY.
2.2 How to contact us
You can contact our BASS team by telephone, email, post or in person at any Pool Facility as detailed on the Bradford Aquatic Website as amended from time to time.
2.3 How we may contact you
If we have to contact you we will do so by email to you but otherwise only if necessary by telephone or post using the details you provided to us in the Application Form or subsequently in Writing from time to time.
3. Our Contract with you
3.1 How we will Contract with you
A Contract for the provision of Swimming Services by the Council to a Member will be entered into only once you have completed all the following, namely handed in your signed and correctly completed Application Form at your Pool Facility, you have received a Notice from the Council confirming what available Swimming Services you have been allocated and you have confirmed in Writing to us within 5 Working Days that you accept that allocation.
3.2 The Agreement between us
The Council agrees to comply with the Council's obligations under these Contract Conditions and provide the allocated Swimming Services to the Member and the Consumer agrees to pay the Fees, inform the Council of any changes to the information provided in the Application form from time to time and that the Member will comply with these Contract Conditions, the Customer Conduct Code and the Swim Wear Policy.
3.3 If we cannot enter into a Contract with you
If we are unable to enter into a Contract with you we will inform you of the reasons for this. This might be because of, for example but not limited to, where you have been placed on a waiting list, there is unexpected limits on our resources which we could not reasonably plan for, we have identified an error in the Fee or description of the Swimming Services, the Council considers that the proposed Member is not eligible to be a member of BASS or the Council has entered into a previous BASS membership contract between the Council and the proposed Consumer which the Council ended because of any of the grounds set out at clause 8.1. In all these circumstances we will not charge you any Fee.
3.4 We only provide Services within a restricted area
We promote and provide the Swimming Services only at the Pool Facilities within the administrative area of the district of Bradford in the UK.
4. Your rights to make changes
If you wish to request a change to the Swimming Services required, please contact us. We will let you know if the change is possible. If it is possible we will let you know about any changes to the Fee, the Pool Facility or the dates and times of the amended Swimming Services or anything else which would be necessary as a result of your request and will ask you to confirm within 7 days whether you wish to go ahead and make that change effective.
5. Our rights to make changes
5.1 Minor changes to the Swimming Services
We may make minor changes to the Swimming Services, for example to reflect changes in any relevant laws and regulatory requirements, amend the opening times of Pool Facilities or temporarily withdraw Swimming Services at any time if the Council requires the Pool Facilities for swimming galas, competitions, in connection with the Council undertaking any alteration or maintenance works due to industrial action, to amend a clear and obvious error in the Fee charged under clause 10.3 or any other reasonable reason. Members will be given general notice of such changes as soon as practicable and the Council will issue any relevant Fee credits only against Fees for future Swimming Services.
5.2 More significant changes to the Swimming Services and these Contract Conditions
Within the Contract Period we may also need to make changes to the scope of the Swimming Services or these Contract Conditions and which may affect the Fee but if we do so we will notify you and we shall not proceed with performance of the Contract until you agree the changes or end the Contract before the changes take effect if you do not wish to continue with it. For example, there may need to be an increase in the Fee due to additional expenditure or staffing required to perform the Swimming Services or an increase in inflation and therefore the RPI.
6. Providing the Swimming Services
6.1 When we will provide the Swimming Services
We will perform the Swimming Services for the Member from the Commencement Date until either you end the Contract as set out in clause 7 or we end the Contract by Notice to you as described in clause 8.
6.2 We are not responsible for delays outside our control
If our performance of the Swimming Services is affected by any events outside our control then we will contact you as soon as possible by Notice to let you know and we will take steps to minimise the effect of any delay. Provided we do this we will not be liable for delays caused by those events.
6.3 The Swimming Services are subject to availability
When your Application Form is approved the Council will give Notice to the Consumer allocating the available dates, times and Pool Facility or informing you that the Member has been placed on a waiting list but who will be removed from the list when a place does become available and the Council has made three abortive attempts to contact, or receive a response from, the Member.
6.4 We have a right to withdraw Swimming Services
The Council reserves the right to withdraw Swimming Services for the reasons set out at clause 5.1 and to provide replacement instructors from time to time when necessary
6.5 You will be issued with a BASS Membership Card
This will be issued to a Member when the Fee has been paid, which:
6.5.1 will remain the property of the Council;
6.5.2 will be required to be replaced at the Consumer's expense at the rate referred to on the Bradford Aquatics Website from time to time if it is damaged, mislaid, lost or stolen; and
6.5.3 must be produced by the Member upon demand this of the Council's employees or agents.
6.6 The Council reserves the right at any time to request any Member or prospective Member to be referred to their general medical practitioner for advice or a report
if the Council, by its Bradford Aquatics manager, considers that in view of the disclosed medical condition or disability of the Member there are reasonable medical concerns that the Member's participation in the intended Swimming Services may adversely affect the Member's health.
7. Your rights to end the Contract
7.1 You have a right to cancel the Contract within the Cancellation Period:
7.1.1 you may contact us within 14 days of the Commencement Date to cancel the Contract without giving any reason so long as your decision to cancel is sent to us to us in a clear statement in Writing.
7.1.2 if you cancel this Contract by way of clause 7.1.1 above we will reimburse to you all payments received from you after deducting the Fees incurred for any Swimming Services you have already received.
7.1.3 we will make the reimbursement without undue delay and not later than 14 days after the day on which we received notice to cancel this Contract.
7.1.4 we will make the reimbursement by way of a cheque sent by post to the address set out in the Application Form unless we have agreed otherwise.
7.2 What happens if you have good reason for ending the Contract
If you are ending the Contract for any of the reasons in 7.2.1 below, the Contract will end on the day on which you sent to us a Notice of the cancellation and we will reimburse to you all payments received from you in advance after deducting any unpaid Fee incurred for the Swimming Services you have already received before you have communicated to us your Notice of ending the Contract.
7.2.1 The relevant reasons are:
7.2.1.1 we have told you about a future change to the scope of the Swimming Services or these Contract Conditions which you do not agree to (see clause 5.2);
7.2.1.2 we have told you about an error in the Fee or description of the Swimming Services or our intention to transfer our obligations under the Contract to another organisation and you do not wish to proceed (see causes 10.3 and 13.1);
7.2.1.3 you have a legal right to end the Contract because of something we have done wrong.
7.3 What happens if you end the Contract without a good reason
If, after the Cancellation Period, you are ending the Contract other than for one of the reasons set out in clause 7.2.1 then the Contract will end after the 30th day after you notified us by a clear statement in Writing of your intention to end the Contract (the "Termination Date") and we will reimburse to you any balance due to you from any payments received from you after this deducting all Fees payable in respect of Swimming Services received up to and including the Termination Date.
8. Our rights to end or suspend the Contract.
8.1 We may end the Contract if you break it
We may end the Contract at any time by Notice to you and reimburse you as referred to at clause 7.1.2 for any of the following reasons:
8.1.1 the Consumer repeatedly breaks the Contract Conditions, the Customer Code of Conduct and/or the Swim Wear Policy.
8.1.2 the Consumer does not, within a reasonable time of us asking for it, provide us with information that is necessary for us to provide the Swimming Services.
8.1.3 the Member's BASS Membership Card is used by any person other than the Member to gain access to a Pool Facility.
8.1.4 the Member has been suspended by the Council for more than a total of 12 Weeks.
8.1.5 the Consumer has verbally or physically abused or intimidated our staff or other visitors at the Pool Facility or has caused or instigated damage intentionally or recklessly to Council property at any Pool Facility.
8.1.6 there has been a relevant error made in the Fee under clause 10.3.
8.1.7 in the absence of, or contrary to, any written medical report or advice requested under clause 6.6, a Member continues to receive Swimming Services which in the reasonable opinion of the Bradford Aquatic Manager poses a significant risk to the Member's health.
8.2 You must compensate us if you break the Contract
If we end the Contract for any reason set out in clause 8.1, the Contract will end on the date which we set out in a Notice to you and we shall reimburse to you all payments received from you after deducting the Fees incurred for any Swimming Services you have already received and any quantifiable and reasonably foreseeable damages the Council may have sustained as a result of your breaking the Contract.
8.3 Our Right to Suspend the Contract
The Council has a right to suspend the Member's BASS Membership for any of the following reasons, if the Consumer:
8.3.1 repeatedly fails to honour Direct Debit payments and the suspension will continue until all the arrears have been paid; and/or
8.3.2 has failed to respond to any Council notification or request by a stipulated timescale and the suspension will continue until the Consumer has responded.
8.4 Your right to Complain
If you disagree that the Contract should end or about any damages deducted as required under these Contract Conditions you have the right to complain under clause 9.
9. If there is a problem with the Contract or the Swimming Services
9.1 How to tell us about problems
If you have a complaint concerning the Contract or Swimming Services provided by the Council this may be best resolved by utilising the following BASS complaints procedure.
9.1.1 communicate with us initially in one of the ways set out in clause 2.2.
9.1.3 if you are unhappy with the way we handled your complaint then tell the person you have dealt with that you wish to have the complaint reviewed by another member of the BASS team who will arrange for your complaint to be investigated further and we will aim to give you a written reply within 15 Working Days. If we need longer to look at your complaint we will let you know.
9.1.4 if you are still unhappy about the way we have handled your complaint you can ask us in Writing that the Bradford Aquatics manager review the original decision. We will contact you and tell you how long the review will take to deal with and confirm his decision in Writing. If the complaint relates to the Council ending the Contract or any damages claimed under clause 8, the complaint will be treated as an appeal and heard at a hearing in person and the decision will be sent to you in Writing within 14 days of the hearing date.
9.1.5 if we are not able to resolve your complaint under this procedure then we will send you in Writing information regarding your rights to obtain independent advice in resolving your dispute through the courts or to refer the matter to the Local Government Ombudsman or an Approved Body providing an Alternative Dispute Resolution Service.
10. Price and payment
10.1 Where to find the Fees for the Swimming Services
The Fees for the Swimming Services are those displayed at Pool Facilities or on the Bradford Aquatic Website from time to time unless we have agreed other Fees in Writing. We take all reasonable care to ensure that the Fees advised to you are correct. However please see clause 10.3 for what happens if we discover an error in the Fees which were sent to you.
10.2 We will pass on to you any applicable charges to VAT or changes in the rate of VAT and increases in the RPI
If VAT becomes chargeable or the rate of VAT changes during the Contract Period, we will adjust the Fee that you pay unless you have paid for the Swimming Services before the charge or change in the rate of VAT takes effect. The Council's VAT registration number is 180 8082 62. Fees will be reviewed on the 1 April and 1 October annually and if applicable these may be increased to reflect any increases in the RPI from the RPI at the previous review date.
10.3 What happens if we got the Fee wrong
It is always possible that despite our efforts some of the Swimming Services we provide may be incorrectly priced. We will normally check Fees before we send Fee details to you but if we identify any error we will inform you of the correct Fee before you sign the Application Form. Where you sign an Application form which includes a Fee error we shall notify you of the correct Fee by way of a permitted change under clause 5.1 and otherwise reserve the right to end the Contract. You may end the Contract if within 14 days of such notification you do not want to continue with the Contract.
10.4 When you must pay and how you must pay
10.4.1 Unless the Council otherwise consents in Writing all Fees must be paid in advance before any Swimming Services are provided to a Member and shall be paid 12 Weeks in advance for all Swimming Courses.
10.4.2 subject to clause 10.4.1 and unless the Council otherwise consents in Writing, Swimming Courses shall be paid by way of Monthly Direct Debit only, unless there are exceptional circumstances, on either the 5th or 15th of the Month as designat

title: Diving | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Bradford Aquatics delivers a diving programme that includes both learn to dive and competitive squad training.
Learn to Dive Scheme
The learn to dive scheme operates at both Shipley Pool and Eccleshill Pool.
Beginners/Intermediate: 30 minute lesson per week covering our level 1, level 2 and level 3 diving awards.
Advanced: 60 minute lesson per week covering our level 4, level 5 and level 6 diving awards.
Adult beginner: 45 minute lesson per week for divers age 16+ who are new to diving.
To take part in the learn to dive scheme you must a minimum of 6 years old and be able to confidently swim a minimum of 25m in deep water. Participants also must be able to climb in and out of the pool over a raised poolside edge unaided and without the use of steps.
During the school holidays we aim to deliver intensive courses of diving lessons. The intensive courses normally run for 60 minutes per day Monday to Friday. Courses include beginner and intermediate level courses at Shipley and Eccleshill Pools and introductory ‘Flip n Fun’ diving courses at Ilkley Pool.
Bradford Aquatics Elite Diving Training Scheme
Bradford Aquatics deliver a training programme that enables divers to train and compete from pre-competition fast track groups, through to national and international level competitors. Our pathway aims to provide progression through a variety of levels of diving allowing athletes to achieve their potential within the sport.
More information on the Elite Training Scheme can be found on the Bradford Aquatics Competition Development Programme page.
City of Bradford Esprit Diving Club
In order for the divers within the Diving Scheme to compete, they must become members of a Diving Club that is affiliated to Swim England. The divers must register, through the club, with both the Swim England North East Region, and the Swim England Nationally. The registration fee is dependent on the level of competition that the diver attends.
For more information please visit the City of Bradford Esprit Diving Club website.

title: Diving squad criteria | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Diving squad criteria
These Squad criteria and reviewed annually and may be changed in August to ensure the best use of available pool space or all divers.
In exceptional circumstances divers maybe moved into a squad when they do not meet the exact criteria and an individual training plan designed for divers' particular needs. This decision is made and agreed between the Diving Development Manager, Diving Development Coach and the Bradford Aquatics Manager and may also involve discussions with the parents or guardians and divers.
Please note that some training could be cancelled due to events or unforeseen circumstances. This has been reflected in the price per month.
For each Squad the following equipment is required:
Swimming trunks or swimming costume
Shorts and T-shirt for dryland training
Trainers (Manningham Dryland sessions)
Please speak to the Squad Coach if any difficulties with this arise.
Squad description and objectives
The squad is for divers who have completed the learn to dive scheme or been identified by coaches as having potential to become a competitive diver. The aims and objectives of the squad are on fundamentals, enjoyment, technique and skill, learning how to take part in competitive squad style training sessions.
At this stage, divers will not yet compete but will learn the basic skills required to take part in introductory level diving competitions.
There are currently 3 groups of Foundation Squad divers, this will be reviewed as required to meet the needs of the scheme.
Divers will be invited to join the Foundation squad when completing level 4 of the learn to dive scheme.
Divers maybe invited to join the Foundation Squad before completing level 4 of the learn to dive scheme if they have demonstrated the following within learn to dive classes:
Streamline to a fair standard on push offs on the front and back.
Perform fly kick underwater to a reasonable standard on the front and back.
Show the basics of effective stroke drills on 3 different strokes.
Perform turns to a satisfactory standard on 3 different strokes and the 3 IM turns.
Show a basic understanding of reading a pace clock.
While in Foundation Squad
Divers will take part in land-based training to develop their physical and technical skills.
Divers will learn and develop the basic skills and techniques required to take part in diving competitions.
Divers arrive on time for the commencement of each session.
Divers will demonstrate a positive attitude towards training, to coaches and their peers.
Divers will arrive at training sessions with the correct and appropriate kit.
Divers will be reviewed to move to Development Squad or Teen Squad on a continual basis.
Divers will be eligible for selection to Development Squad if they are 11 years or younger and completed the skills needed to take part in introductory level diving competitions for their age group.
Divers will be eligible for selection to the Teen Squad if they are aged 12 to 15 years.
See entry criteria for Development Squad or Teen Squad
To develop divers’ skills in both dryland and in the pool learning how to compete. Divers will be expected to take part in competitions of the appropriate level.
Overall skill is of high importance and the main issues that will be considered are posture and take off techniques, line up sequences, body positioning and entries. Divers must be able to complete the skills required for their age group to take part in entry level Novice/Skills competitions.
Divers will be reviewed to move to Competition Squad on a continual basis throughout the year.
Divers will only be eligible to join Competition Squad from the age of 8 upwards for Males and Females
Divers will only be considered to move to Competition Squad if they have taken part in regional skills championships, or equivalent level event.
If divers do not achieve Competition Squad standard by 14 years of age they will exit Development Squad and be recommended to continue in the Teen Squad.
Divers will arrive at training sessions with the correct and appropriate kit
See entry criteria for Competition Squad
Squad description and objectives
The squad is for divers aged between 8 to 16. The aims and objectives of the squad are for divers to qualify and compete at National Skills Finals, whilst developing skills to move compete in Age group level competitions.
Divers must have competed in North East Regional Skills or equivalent level event.
Divers must have achieved or demonstrated the ability to achieve the standard to National Skills Finals qualification for their age group.
Age group National Skills Qualification Standard
Group E (8/9 years) 240 points
Group D (10/11 years) 255 points
Group C (12/13 years) 270 points
Group B (14/15 years) 265 points
Group A (16 - 18 years) 1m springboard 170 points
3m springboard 175 points
While in Competition Squad
Divers will arrive on time for the commencement of each session.
It is desirable that divers will have a achieved a national skills qualification score.
Divers will demonstrate a positive attitude towards training, the coaches and their peers.
Divers must show a commitment to attending regular competitions including club invitational and/or regional age group competitions.
Divers will arrive at training sessions with the correct and appropriate kit.
Divers will move to Performance Development Squad when they reach the required ability, criteria and age (See entry criteria for Performance Development Squad).
Divers will lose their place in the squad if they fail to attend National Skills finals when they have achieved the qualification standard.
Performance Development Group
Divers to have competitive success at National Age Group Championships, and prepare aiming to compete at Elite Junior level competitions.
The squad is divers aged 12 years and over and have achieved the qualification standard for Swim England National Age Group Championships.
Divers aged 18 years plus will lose their place in the squad if they are not achieving the recommended standard to compete at senior level events.
Squad description and objectives
Teen squad is a mainly recreational training squad for divers aged 12 to 17 years who have completed the learn to dive scheme, but do not meet the entry criteria for a competitive level squad; or have chosen not to compete.
Divers must be age 12 to 17 years and completed the learn to dive scheme.
Divers must have taken part in Foundation Squad before being invited to join the Teen Squad.
Divers will work with coach to develop their skills and achieve individual goals in diving.
Divers will take part in both land based and pool skills during training sessions.
Divers aged 18 years plus will no longer be able to train in the Teen Squad and will be invited to join the Masters Squad.
The ages of divers in the squad are 16+ years. Divers should have either been competitive divers previously or competed Adult Beginner diving lessons. In Masters Squad divers are encouraged and recommended to compete in Masters Competitions, however they will work with the coaches to develop their skills and achieve their individual goals.

title: Elite training code of conduct for children | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Code of conduct for children
As a member of Bradford Aquatics elite training programme, we understand you have the right to:
Enjoy the time you spend with us and know that you are safe.
Be told who you can talk to if something’s not right.
Be involved and contribute towards decisions where appropriate during training sessions.
Be respected by us and other team members and be treated fairly.
Feel welcomed, valued and not judged based on your race, gender, sexuality, faith or ability.
Be encouraged and develop your swimming, para-swimming, diving, artistic swimming, water polo and open water swimming skills with our help and support.
Be looked after if there’s an accident or injury and have your parents/guardians informed, where appropriate.
As a member of Bradford Aquatics elite training programme, we expect you to:
Keep yourself safe by listening to your coach or facility staff, behave responsibly and speak out when something isn’t right.
Take care of our equipment and premises as if they were your own.
Make it to training on time and if you’re running late, let the coaches know.
Make your coach or teacher aware if you have any difficulties attending training or competitions.
Not wander off or leave training or a competition without telling your coach.
Bring the right kit to training.
Follow the rules of the facility and squad at all times.
Respect the privacy of others especially in the changing rooms.
Make training a fun, happy, friendly and welcoming place to be.
Respect and celebrate difference in our club or activity and not discriminate against anyone else on the grounds of age, gender, race, sexual orientation, faith, or ability.
Understand that the use of abusive or inappropriate language, bullying, physical violence, or any other behaviour which hurts others will not be tolerated.
Follow the rules of the training facilities. (for example, no mobile phones on pool, and changing areas).
Understand that poor behaviour may result in disciplinary action against you. Any behaviour which may be a criminal offence will be reported to police.
Report any incidents of bullying or unkind behaviour to the club, even if you’re just a witness.
Treat other children with respect and appreciate that everyone has a different level of skill or talent.
Support and encourage your teammates, tell them when they’ve done well and be there for them when they are struggling.
Respect the facility staff and coaching team.
Breaches of the code of conduct
Breaches of this Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary action being taken against you by the Bradford Aquatics Scheme.
Any breaches of this code will be dealt with as follows:
Verbal warning from the manager: yellow card.
Written warning from the manager: yellow card 2.
Written removal from the scheme: red card.
Depending on the severity of the incident or behaviour, the scheme has the right to go straight to a red card if it is deemed that the behaviour warrants exclusion from the Council scheme and the Club.

As a parent or guardian of a club member we understand you have the right to:

Know the procedure should your child be involved in an accident or become injured.
Make a complaint to management.

Remember that children get a wide range of benefits from participating in one of our sports, like making friends, getting exercise, and developing skills. It’s not all about wins and losses.

Talk to your child and ensure they understand the rules of the scheme and the sport.
Ensure your child understands their Code of Conduct.

title: KS2 swimming lessons information leaflet | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
Parents information leaflet for pupils attending KS2 School Swimming Lessons
Hints and tips for parents with children having school swimming lessons
Appropriate swimwear should be worn by your child for the swimming lesson
It is strongly recommended that children wear close fitting costumes / trunks or fully lined swimming shorts.
Only clothing made and sold for the specific purposes of swimming is permitted, however, for recognised medical, cultural and religious reasons it is acceptable for close fitting Lycra leggings etc. to be worn in addition to the above.
Please note, the categories below are not intended to be prescriptive. Where appropriate, swimwear may be chosen from either category.
Examples of male swimwear which would be considered acceptable under this guidance
Examples of female swimwear which would be considered acceptable under this guidance
Emergency procedures
On the first visit to the pool your child will be taken through all the Emergency Procedures. This includes a safety talk delivered by one of the swimming teachers and will include pupils listening to the pool alarm and the fire alarm.
Hygiene at the swimming pool
Pupils should go to the toilet before going onto poolside, pupils with long hair should wear swimming caps or tie their hair back. If your child has had diarrhoea they should not swim for two weeks.
It is recommended that jewellery should not be worn during the swimming lesson. If the swimming teacher is of the opinion that your child is wearing an item of jewellery that could be a hazard to your child, or any other child, he/she will be asked to remove it before entering the water. The swimming teacher will not accept responsibility for any item of jewellery and it should be given to the school teacher.
Your child does not have to wear swimming goggles, however, if your child is experienced at using goggles they can be worn, but if wearing the goggles leads to your child delaying or disrupting the lesson by playing with them he / she will be asked to remove them. Please be aware that goggles can cause eye injuries and manufacturer’s instructions must be followed.
Your child will be provided with armbands if necessary. They will experience swimming in shallow water and in deep water with as many aids as necessary to make them feel safe.
They will learn a variety of skills.
Your child may also experience swimming in their clothes during their swimming lesson. Clothes must be clean, light weight and easily removed.
There are a range of badges and certificates that your child can achieve during their swimming lesson and these are reported to your child’s school teacher throughout the year and badges can be bought if wished through your child’s school teacher.
Key Stage 2 National Curriculum for Swimming
The main aim of the school swimming lesson is for your child to enjoy swimming and for them to achieve their Key Stage 2 National Curriculum for Swimming, which is:
Swim 10 metres Breast stroke
Swim 10 metres Back crawl
Swim 10 metres Front crawl
(2 out of the 3 strokes required)
If your child can or does reach their Key Stage 2 National Curriculum for swimming during their swimming lesson there are a range of other awards and aquatic skills that can be offered to your child.
Download or print a copy of this information
You can download a copy of this leaflet (PDF).

text:
Sport and activities
RLSS National Pool Lifeguard Qualification
Bradford Aquatics run National Pool Lifeguard Qualifications courses throughout the year.
This is a nationally recognised qualification in the leisure industry for swimming pool lifeguards. It provides skills in swimming pool supervision, intervention and rescue, first aid and resuscitation.
Be 16 or over on the date of the assessment.
Jump and dive into deep water.
Swim 50 metres in no more than 60 seconds (demonstrating a recognised stroke).
To swim continuously 100m on front and 100m on back.
In deep water, tread water for 30 seconds.
Surface dive to the floor of the pool (12 foot 6 inches) without hearing or ear problems.
Climb out of the pool unaided without using a ladder or steps where the pool design permits.
To guarantee your place, you will need to show us these skills during a short assessment. This will take place from two to four weeks before the start of the course. We recommend that you practice these skills before you are assessed.

title: Swim squad criteria | Bradford Council
text:
Sport and activities
These Squad criteria and reviewed annually and may be changed in August to ensure the best use of available pool space or all swimmers.
In exceptional circumstances swimmers maybe moved into a squad when they do not meet the exact criteria and an individual training plan designed for swimmers particular needs. This decision is made at the Competitive team meetings and will be agreed between the Senior Coach, Development Coach and the Bradford Aquatics Manager and may also involve discussions with the parents or guardians and swimmers.
Please note that some training could be cancelled due to events / unforeseen circumstances this has been reflected in the price per month.
For each Squad the following equipment is required:
Swimming trunks or swimming costume
Swimming cap (if you normally wear one)
Swimming goggles and a spare pair
Hand and finger paddles (if you own them)
Fins (of the correct size)
Please speak to the Squad Coach if any difficulties with this arise.
Squad description and objectives
The squad is for swimmers aged 7 to 12 for both males and females. The aims and objectives of the squad are on fundamentals, enjoyment, technique and skill, a wide range of stroke drills will be used and a firm focus will be placed streamlining, underwater fly kick and turn techniques.
At this age, swimmers will be encouraged to compete (mainly graded meets with their local clubs, will be targeted) and Grassroots meets will be available for squad members up to the age of 9 and squad members will be encouraged to compete in these meets with their local clubs.
The number of swimmers in the squad will be 42. (This number will be reviewed annually).
Swimmers will be taken into Rising Stars Squad from the local clubs and from Talent ID spotting within the Bradford Aquatic swimming lessons. The local club coaches shall be consulted with regard to any intake of new swimmers from their particular clubs.
Swimmers must be of the age as stated in the squad description.
Swimmers must be competent in swimming 3 different strokes and be able to swim a distance of 200 metres continuously using 1 or more strokes.
Swimmers must show a fair standard of aerobic stamina to be considered for Rising Stars Squad.
Swimmers will only be considered to move in to Rising Stars Squad if they can perform the following on a constant ongoing basis:
Streamline to a fair standard on push offs on the front and back.
Perform fly kick underwater to a reasonable standard on the front and back.
Show the basics of effective stroke drills on 3 different strokes.
Perform turns to a satisfactory standard on 3 different strokes and the 3 IM turns.
Show a basic understanding of reading a pace clock.
While in Rising Stars Squad
Swimmers will be encouraged to enter Grassroots competitions when they feel ready.
Swimmers arrive on time for the commencement of each session.
Swimmers will demonstrate a positive attitude towards training, to coaches and their peers.
Swimmers will arrive at training sessions with the correct and appropriate kit.
Swimmers will be reviewed to move to Rising Stars Transition Squad or Junior Development Squad at 3 review points during the year (usually September, Christmas and Easter).
Swimmers will only be eligible to join Rising Stars Transition Squad or Junior Development Squad from the age of 9 upwards for males and females.
If swimmers do not achieve Junior Development Squad standard by 13 years of age they will exit Rising Stars Squad and be recommended continue to swim with their local club.
See entry criteria for Rising Stars Transition Squad or Junior Development Squad
Rising Stars Transition Squad
To prepare swimmers for the Junior Development Squad
The maximum number of swimmers selected for RS Trans Squad is 8.
Overall skill is of high importance and the main issues that will be considered are Streamlining, ability to kick fly underwater to a good standard, stroke technique and turning ability. The Senior Coach and Development Coaches’ decisions are final.
Swimmers will be reviewed to move to Junior Development Squad at 3 review points during the year (usually September, Christmas and Easter, if places are available).
Swimmers will only be eligible to join Junior Development Squad from the age of 9 upwards for Males and Females
Swimmers must show a good standard of aerobic stamina to be considered for Junior Development Squad.
Swimmers will only be considered to move to Junior Development Squad if they can perform the following on a constant ongoing basis:
Streamline to high standard on push offs on the front and back.
Perform fly kick underwater to a good standard on the front and back.
Show effective stroke drills on 3 different strokes.
Perform turns to a satisfactory standard on 3 different strokes and the 3 IM turns.
Show a basic understanding of reading a pace clock.
If swimmers do not achieve Junior Development Squad standard by 13 years of age they will exit Rising Stars Squad and be recommended to continue to swim with their local club.
Swimmers will arrive at training sessions with the correct and appropriate kit
See entry criteria for Junior Development Squad
Junior Development Squad
Squad description and objectives
The squad is for swimmers aged between 9 to 15 for both males and females. The aims and objectives of the squad are to develop swimmers for age group (BAGCAT) competitions. A varied range of skills and stroke drills will be implemented, but the focus will be on fundamentals and enjoyment. The maximum number in the squad will be 36 swimmers.
Swimmers must be of the age as stated in the squad description.
Swimmers must have ambitions to achieve N.E.R. qualifying times and above.
To be considered for JD swimmers must be able to demonstrate, on a regular basis:
A good front and back streamlined position when pushing of the walls.
A good fly kick on both front and back when pushing of walls.
Show a satisfactory level of turn skill on all 4 strokes and the 3 IM turns.
Be competent on 3 of the 4 swimming strokes.
Show a satisfactory level of fitness and stamina.
While in Junior Development Squad
Swimmers will attend a minimum of 5 sessions per week, including Saturday mornings.
Swimmers will arrive on time for the commencement of each session.
It is desirable that swimmers will hold a current Yorkshire A. qualifying time.
Swimmers will demonstrate a positive attitude towards training, the coaches and their peers.
Swimmers must show a commitment to morning training to be considered to move into Youth Development Squad.
Attend a minimum of 8 meets per season and enter the correct events as directed by the Senior Coach and Development Coach.
Swimmers will arrive at training sessions with the correct and appropriate kit.
Swimmers will move to Youth Development Transition Squad when they reach the required ability, criteria and age (See entry criteria for Youth Development Squad).
Swimmers will lose their place in the squad if their attendance falls below 4 sessions per week on a more often than not basis and will be recommended to continue their training with the local clubs.
Junior Development Transition Group
To prepare swimmers for the Youth Development Squad
The squad is for swimmers that have reached the age of 13. The squad will not exceed 6 swimmers. The Senior Coaches and Development Coaches decision is final. It is desirable that swimmers hold a minimum of 1 NER QT.
Swimmers will lose their place in the squad if their attendance falls below 5 sessions per week on a more often than not basis and will be recommended to the local clubs.
Will move to Youth Development Squad once they reach the required ability, criteria and age to do so.
Youth Development Squad
Squad description and objectives
Youth Development Squad is the premier squad within the scheme. The maximum number of places available in YD Squad is 26. The aims and objectives of the squad are to develop and prepare swimmers for the National Championships and above such as International competition. An emphasis is also placed on success at Yorkshire S.A. and North East Region A.S.A. events and the progression to these levels through competition in selected open and club meets.
Swimmers must be able to demonstrate a high skill level on all 4 strokes, all turns including Medley turns, streamlining, under water kick skill and a good understanding of using a pace clock.
Swimmers will be reviewed to move to Youth Development Squad at 3 review points during the year (usually September, Christmas and Easter, if places are available).
Swimmers in Youth Development Squad will be aged 14 for both males and females. Younger swimmers can be taken/fast tracked in to Youth Development depending on the swimmers ability, Skill, and requirements. The Senior Coach’s decision will be final regarding this.
It is desirable that swimmers have at least 1 regional qualifying time.
While in Youth Development Squad
The number of required sessions each swimmer attends weekly will be set by the Senior Coach. The Minimum requirement is 6 sessions. Swimmers attending a Competition on a Saturday will be classed as attending training.
Swimmers must show an ongoing commitment to morning training.
Swimmers must attend the Saturday morning session at Eccleshill Pool and take part in the land session after the water session.
Swimmers must attend meets and enter relevant events on a regular basis as directed by the Senior Coach. (Minimum of 6 meets per year). If a swimmer competes on 1 day of a 2 day meet only that will be considered as 1 meet.
Swimmers will arrive on time for sessions and will complete blood flow exercises prior to the commencement of sessions.
Swimmers must complete sessions to the standard required
Swimmers must demonstrate a positive attitude towards training, coaches and their peers.
Swimmers will arrive at training sessions with the correct and appropriate kit
Swimmers are expected to keep an up to date logbook.
Squad description and objectives
There will be 6 places available, for those whom fulfil the criteria below. The aim of the squad will be to fulfil the commitment of 3 to 4 swim sessions per week to fit in around their other training for the cycle and run elements of the Triathlon. It is expected that they will partake in the swim sessions with the aim of improving their speed, stamina and endurance for the swim element of the Triathlon.
It has been decided, that to be eligible to train as a triathlete within the Bradford Aquatics swim training scheme, that the individual must have been selected by the YTA (Yorkshire Triathlon Academy) or the YTS (Yorkshire Talent Squad).
The YTA has qualification times that need to be achieved for the swim, these are for 13 to 15 years a 200m time and for 16 to 19 years a 400m time. See the table below.
Age Female qualification time Male qualification time
14 years 2.25.8 2.20.1
15 years 2.24.4 2.17.4
16 years 5.00.4 4.48.7
17 years 4.57.4 4.43.1
18 years 4.54.5 4.37.5
The YTS allows the swimmer to be just outside the time on the swim or run but to be on the radar to be selected.
Squad description and objectives
The ages of swimmers in the squad are 18+ for males and females.
Bradford Aquatics Competitive Swimming Training Scheme is committed to the competitive development of its participants. Swimmers in Masters Squad are encouraged and recommended to compete in Masters Competitions such as open meets, county, regional and National competition. Its members are also encouraged and recommended to be members of the COBSC. This membership allows individuals to compete in such competitions.
Priority regarding available space at training will be given to the competitive members of the squad.
